From 98d0912e9f841e5529a5b89a972805f34cb1c69d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Minh Nguyen <minhnguyen.080505@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 11:12:39 +0700
Subject: [PATCH] net: skbuff: fix missing zerocopy reference in pskb_carve
 helpers

pskb_carve_inside_header() and pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear() both copy
the old skb_shared_info header into a new buffer via memcpy(), which
includes the destructor_arg pointer (uarg) for MSG_ZEROCOPY skbs.
Neither function calls net_zcopy_get() for the new shinfo, creating an
unaccounted holder: every skb_shared_info with destructor_arg set will
call skb_zcopy_clear() once when freed, but the corresponding
net_zcopy_get() was never called for the new copy. Repeated calls
drive uarg->refcnt to zero prematurely, freeing ubuf_info_msgzc while
TX skbs still hold live destructor_arg pointers.

KASAN reports use-after-free on a freed ubuf_info_msgzc:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in skb_release_data+0x77b/0x810
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff88801574d3e8 by task poc/220

  Call Trace:
   skb_release_data+0x77b/0x810
   kfree_skb_list_reason+0x13e/0x610
   skb_release_data+0x4cd/0x810
   sk_skb_reason_drop+0xf3/0x340
   skb_queue_purge_reason+0x282/0x440
   rds_tcp_inc_free+0x1e/0x30
   rds_recvmsg+0x354/0x1780
   __sys_recvmsg+0xdf/0x180

  Allocated by task 219:
   msg_zerocopy_realloc+0x157/0x7b0
   tcp_sendmsg_locked+0x2892/0x3ba0

  Freed by task 219:
   ip_recv_error+0x74a/0xb10
   tcp_recvmsg+0x475/0x530

The skb consuming the late access still referenced the same uarg via
shinfo->destructor_arg copied by pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear() without
a refcount bump. This has been verified to be reliably exploitable: a
working proof-of-concept achieves full root privilege escalation from
an unprivileged local user on a default kernel configuration.

The fix follows the pattern of pskb_expand_head() which has the same
memcpy/cloned structure. For pskb_carve_inside_header(), net_zcopy_get()
is placed after skb_orphan_frags() succeeds, so the orphan error path
needs no cleanup. For pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear(), net_zcopy_get() is
placed after all failure points and just before skb_release_data(), so
no error path needs cleanup at all -- matching pskb_expand_head() more
closely and avoiding the need for a balancing net_zcopy_put().

Fixes: 6fa01ccd8830 ("skbuff: Add pskb_extract() helper function")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-sonnet-4-6
Signed-off-by: Minh Nguyen <minhnguyen.080505@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260526041240.329462-1-minhnguyen.080505@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/core/skbuff.c b/net/core/skbuff.c
index d247acd447e4..0d3cc115f2e7 100644
--- a/net/core/skbuff.c
+++ b/net/core/skbuff.c
@@ -6833,6 +6833,8 @@ static int pskb_carve_inside_header(struct sk_buff *skb, const u32 off,
 			skb_kfree_head(data);
 			return -ENOMEM;
 		}
+		if (skb_zcopy(skb))
+			net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb));
 		for (i = 0; i < skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags; i++)
 			skb_frag_ref(skb, i);
 		if (skb_has_frag_list(skb))
@@ -6976,6 +6978,8 @@ static int pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear(struct sk_buff *skb, const u32 off,
 		skb_kfree_head(data);
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	}
+	if (skb_zcopy(skb))
+		net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb));
 	skb_release_data(skb, SKB_CONSUMED);
 
 	skb->head = data;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

**File modified:** `net/core/skbuff.c`

**Modifications:**

1. **In `pskb_carve_inside_header()`** (line ~6833):  
   Added a check and reference increment for zerocopy uarg (`net_zcopy_get()`) after `skb_orphan_frags()` succeeds, before taking references on individual frags. This ensures that the new skb_shared_info’s destructor_arg pointer is accounted for.

2. **In `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()`** (line ~6978):  
   Added the same `net_zcopy_get()` call after all failure points and just before `skb_release_data()`. This mirrors the approach in `pskb_expand_head()` and avoids needing cleanup on error paths.

**Relationship:**  
Both functions copy the old `skb_shared_info` (including the zerocopy uarg pointer) via `memcpy()` without calling `net_zcopy_get()` on the new copy. This creates an unaccounted holder, causing premature freeing of the zerocopy buffer when the original skb is freed. The patch adds the missing reference increment in both locations to fix the use-after-free vulnerability. The placement differs slightly due to error-handling structure, but the logical fix is identical.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
memcpy((struct skb_shared_info *)(data + size), skb_shinfo(skb), offsetof(struct skb_shared_info, frags[skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags]));
```
and
```c
memcpy((struct skb_shared_info *)(data + size), skb_shinfo(skb), offsetof(struct skb_shared_info, frags[0]));
```
without a subsequent `net_zcopy_get()` call on the copied `destructor_arg` pointer.

Reason: Both `pskb_carve_inside_header()` and `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()` copy the entire `skb_shared_info` (including the `destructor_arg` for MSG_ZEROCOPY skbs) via `memcpy`. However, they fail to increment the reference count (`net_zcopy_get()`) for the new copy. This creates an unaccounted holder, so when the original SKB is freed and calls `skb_zcopy_clear()`, the `uarg->refcnt` drops prematurely, leading to use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (skb_zcopy(skb))
	net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb));
```
inserted after the `memcpy` and before `skb_release_data()` in both `pskb_carve_inside_header()` and `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()`.

Reason: The added lines check if the SKB uses zerocopy (`skb_zcopy(skb)` is true) and, if so, explicitly increment the reference count (`net_zcopy_get`) on the shared zerocopy metadata. This ensures that the new SKB copy holds a proper reference, preventing premature freeing of the `ubuf_info_msgzc` structure. The placement in `pskb_carve_inside_header()` is after `skb_orphan_frags()` succeeds (so error path cleanup not needed); in `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()` it is placed after all error paths (just before `skb_release_data()`), matching the pattern used in `pskb_expand_head()`.
